source.anchor: standard bounded stopping consequence for a square-integrable real Ito integral; Samplinglib completed-process formulation
source.original_text: Let eta be a progressively measurable real integrand that is square-integrable on a positive finite horizon T, let B be Brownian motion relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, and let tau be a nonnegative stopping time satisfying tau(omega) <= T for every omega. Then the expectation of the completed Ito integral I_tau = integral_0^tau eta_s dB_s is zero. This is the centered value of the constructed real global-L2 Ito process at a bounded stopping time; it is not a general optional-sampling theorem and asserts nothing about unbounded stopping times, local martingales before localization, vector stochastic integration, quadratic variation, or Ito's formula.

theorem integral_itoIntegralProcess_at_boundedStopping_eq_zero
    [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    (eta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (tau : Omega → ℝ≥0)
    (htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration
      (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)))
    (htauT : ∀ omega, tau omega ≤ T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu) :
    ∫ omega, itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega ∂mu = 0

blind_reconstruction.text: 在相同设定下，设 T>0，η 是时间范围 T 内的实值渐进可测 L² 被积过程，B 是相对于 filtration 和有限测度 μ 的实 Brownian 运动，且 filtration 满足通常条件。若 τ:Ω→ℝ≥0 是相对于 filtration 的停止时间并逐点满足 τ≤T，则停止的 Ito 积分具有零均值：∫Ω(∫₀^{τ(ω)}η_s dB_s)dμ(ω)=0。

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.RandomStoppingGeneralIto

/-!
# Mean of a completed Itô process at a bounded stopping time

For a progressive square-integrable integrand on a finite horizon, the
completed Itô process evaluated at a stopping time bounded by that horizon is
integrable and has mean zero.

The proof applies the martingale mean identity to the completed Itô process of
the stopped integrand.  The completed random-stopping theorem then identifies
its terminal value with evaluation of the original continuous process at the
stopping time.  No optional-sampling theorem beyond the deterministic-time
martingale identity is required.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory
namespace TechnicalLemmas
namespace StochasticProcesses
namespace BoundedStoppedItoMean

open MeasureTheory Set
open scoped NNReal

open BrownianMotion ItoIntegralProcess ProgressiveL2 ProgressiveL2Stopping
  RandomStoppingGeneralIto StoppingTime

variable {Omega : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace Omega}
  {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 m} {mu : Measure Omega} {T : ℝ≥0}
  {B : ℝ≥0 → Omega → ℝ}

/-- The completed Itô process is integrable when evaluated at a stopping time
that is pointwise bounded by its construction horizon. -/
theorem itoIntegralProcess_at_boundedStopping_integrable
    [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    (eta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (tau : Omega → ℝ≥0)
    (htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration
      (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)))
    (htauT : ∀ omega, tau omega ≤ T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu) :
    Integrable
      (fun omega => itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega) mu := by
  let _ : IsProbabilityMeasure mu := hB.isProbabilityMeasure
  let stoppedEta := stop eta (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) htau
  have hterminal :
      terminalRepresentative stoppedEta hT hB =ᵐ[mu]
        (fun omega => itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega) := by
    exact (itoIntegralTerminal_stop_ae eta hT tau htau htauT hB hUsual)
  exact (terminalRepresentative_integrable stoppedEta hT hB).congr hterminal

/-- The completed Itô process has mean zero when evaluated at a stopping time
that is pointwise bounded by its construction horizon. -/
theorem integral_itoIntegralProcess_at_boundedStopping_eq_zero
    [IsFiniteMeasure mu]
    (eta : ProgressiveL2Integrand filtration mu T) (hT : 0 < T)
    (tau : Omega → ℝ≥0)
    (htau : IsChewiStoppingTime filtration
      (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)))
    (htauT : ∀ omega, tau omega ≤ T)
    (hB : IsBrownianMotionWithFiltration B filtration mu)
    (hUsual : SatisfiesUsualConditions filtration mu) :
    ∫ omega, itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega ∂mu = 0 := by
  let _ : IsProbabilityMeasure mu := hB.isProbabilityMeasure
  let stoppedEta := stop eta (fun omega => (tau omega : WithTop ℝ≥0)) htau
  have hmartingale :
      Martingale (itoIntegralProcess stoppedEta hT hB hUsual) filtration mu :=
    itoIntegralProcess_martingale stoppedEta hT hB hUsual
  have hterminalMean :
      ∫ omega, terminalRepresentative stoppedEta hT hB omega ∂mu = 0 := by
    have hmean := hmartingale.setIntegral_eq (show (0 : ℝ≥0) ≤ T from bot_le)
      (MeasurableSet.univ : MeasurableSet[filtration 0] Set.univ)
    have hprocessMean :
        ∫ omega, itoIntegralProcess stoppedEta hT hB hUsual T omega ∂mu = 0 := by
      simpa only [Measure.restrict_univ, itoIntegralProcess_at_zero,
        Pi.zero_apply, integral_zero] using hmean.symm
    exact integral_congr_ae
      (terminalRepresentative_ae_eq_actual stoppedEta hT hB hUsual) |>.trans hprocessMean
  calc
    ∫ omega, itoIntegralProcess eta hT hB hUsual (tau omega) omega ∂mu =
        ∫ omega, terminalRepresentative stoppedEta hT hB omega ∂mu := by
          apply integral_congr_ae
          exact (itoIntegralTerminal_stop_ae eta hT tau htau htauT hB hUsual).symm
    _ = 0 := hterminalMean

end BoundedStoppedItoMean
end StochasticProcesses
end TechnicalLemmas
end AutoSamplingTheory

candidate_publication_context.statement: For a progressive square-integrable real integrand on a positive finite horizon, evaluating its completed continuous Ito process at a nonnegative stopping time bounded pointwise by the horizon gives an integrable random variable of expectation zero.
assumptions: A progressive L2 integrand on a positive NNReal horizon T.
A Brownian motion relative to the filtration and ambient measure, and the usual filtration conditions.
An NNReal-valued stopping time tau with tau(omega)≤T for every omega.
An ambient finite-measure instance, already entailed by the Brownian probability contract and used by the completed-process API.

obligations.label: Transfer terminal L2 integrability to bounded random-time evaluation
Derive zero expectation from the stopped-integrand martingale and random-stopping identity

lesson.title: A completed Ito process has mean zero at a bounded stopping time
lesson.statement: Under the same global L2, Brownian, usual-filtration, stopping-time, and pointwise horizon-bound assumptions, the integral of the completed Ito process evaluated at tau is zero.
assumptions: eta is a Samplinglib ProgressiveL2Integrand on a positive NNReal horizon T.
B is Brownian with respect to the filtration and measure, and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions.
tau is an NNReal-valued stopping time with tau(omega)≤T for every omega.
The theorem concerns the library's actual completed continuous Ito process, not an arbitrary process supplied together with a martingale premise.

steps.title: Use the stopped-integrand martingale
steps.text: The completed Ito process of the stopped integrand is a martingale and starts exactly at zero, including on the patched exceptional set.

steps.title: Compare deterministic times zero and T
steps.text: The martingale set-integral identity on the whole sample space makes the expectation at T equal the expectation at zero, hence zero.
steps.lean: Use Martingale.setIntegral_eq with the universal measurable set.

steps.title: Transfer to the bounded stopping time
steps.text: The terminal representative agrees almost everywhere both with J_T and with the original completed process I evaluated at tau. Integral congruence transfers the zero expectation.

lesson.lean_statement: The conclusion is the literal Bochner integral equality for random-time evaluation of the constructed completed Ito process.
lesson.lean_proof: The proof applies deterministic-time preservation of martingale expectation to the stopped integrand and then rewrites the terminal value using the two existing almost-everywhere consistency theorems.
